slides.prompt: How did Covid-19 change the world?
slides.hint: On Monday, we used four checks to choose a missing sentence.
slides.notes: 60-min Tue lesson, sl_t1. Opening hook for Module p.69. Monday one-liner only, no reteaching. Outcomes (teacher-kept): read the passage clearly for PBD; use 6 new words in own sentences.

items: Daily life changed, and people helped one another.
Good hygiene and technology still help us stay connected.
slides.notes: Prime the passage ideas in simple vocabulary. Partner talk 1 min: which change still helps us today? Point and say why.

slides.prompt: What does this family scene show about staying connected?
slides.alt: A family spending time together at home
slides.notes: PURPOSEFUL VISUAL (~2 min). Reused local family scene as a concrete bridge to cooperation and staying connected at home. It supports discussion but does not reveal any target-word answer.

slides.answer: Strong again after a difficult time.
slides.feedback: People and communities can become resilient after a difficult time.
slides.notes: Elicit first, then reveal. Word 1 of 6.

slides.feedback: Vaccines can reduce the severity of an illness.
slides.notes: Word 2 of 6. Sets up the weak-vs-strong slide.

slides.feedback: The ending -let can mean small: droplet, booklet, leaflet.
slides.notes: Word 3 of 6. -let spotlight per SOT: drop + -let, book + -let, leaf + -let.

slides.feedback: The pandemic caused a break in normal life.
The pandemic was a significant event in history.
slides.notes: Word 6 of 6. Module gloss follows p.69. Misconception: pupils copy definitions — enforce show, don't repeat.

slides.prompt: Mix a word with an idea. Make a sentence.

pairs.meaning: strong again after a difficult time

slides.frame: Use because or so. Your sentence must show the word's meaning.
slides.notes: Required all-words synthesis. Keep all six word–meaning pairs visible. Select any word and idea, then invite pupils to accept, improve or reject the combination with a reason. Some combinations need imaginative context; that judgement is part of the mix-and-match task.

slides.prompt: Which sentence shows the meaning of severity?

columns.label: B
columns.text: Vaccines reduced the severity of illness, so fewer people became very sick.

slides.hint: Look for an action and a result.
slides.notes: Frame: word + action + detail + because/so + result. Explain that A gives a definition but does not show the word in use. Copy the habit, not the sentence.

items: The teacher chooses pupils with the randomizer.
Use one target word in your own sentence.
slides.notes: Teacher goes around testing against LS 3.1.5 (read the article) and LS 3.1.4 (word meanings); about 8 readers. Passage stays in the book (copyright). No names in artifacts.

slides.prompt: Write one sentence that shows a word's meaning
slides.task: Choose one word: resilient, severity, droplet, vital, disruption or significant. Write one sentence about your life or school that shows its meaning.
slides.frame: Word + action + detail + because / so + result.
slides.notes: 5 min silent exit. Bridge: Thursday turns the p.70 handwashing essay into an information-transfer table. Collect short/long books after.
